title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 749-757 of the sequel to La Longue Marche). Grothendieck is axiomatising a 'Lie development' (here 'tour de Lie') of a 'Teichmüller-Galois structure'. That structure is a triple of profinite groups Π ⊂ 𝔖 ⊂ M (geometric, intermediate and arithmetic). Π and 𝔖 are profinite completions of discrete groups Π_0 and 𝔖_0, presumably Teichmüller-type groups. M also carries the Galois action and has no discrete model. The 'development' consists of group schemes of finite type over S_0 = Spec Z, written Π, 𝔖, M (underlined), together with homomorphisms Π_0 → Π(Z), etc.

On the previous page Grothendieck forms the component group schemes γ = Π/Π° (and likewise for 𝔖 and M). He asks that they be constant.

(59) Each γ is the constant group scheme on a finite group γ_Π, γ_𝔖, γ_M. These finite groups are quotients of Π, 𝔖, M; that is, the composite Π → Π(Ẑ) → γ is surjective.

(60) The γ's form a chain of homomorphisms γ_Π → γ_𝔖 → γ_M. He corrected 'suite exacte' to 'suite d'homs', since it is not exact.

(61) The 'third isomorphism theorem' diagram: four right-exact sequences. Here Σ = 𝔖/Π, N = M/Π and T = M/𝔖, with γ_Σ → γ_N → γ_T → 1.

Key construction. Because each γ is constant (γ_Π)_{S_0}, the group Π(Ẑ) = ∏_p Π(Z_p) maps to ∏_p γ_Π. Define Π^Δ(Ẑ) as the preimage of the diagonal γ_Π ⊂ ∏_p γ_Π. These are the adelic points whose connected component is the same at every prime; the Δ stands for 'diagonal'. This is a closed subgroup. Every Z-point has the same component at every p, so Π(Z) ⊂ Π^Δ(Ẑ). Π is the profinite completion of Π_0, and Π_0 maps into Π(Z). Hence the continuous map Π → Π(Ẑ) automatically factors through Π^Δ(Ẑ), and likewise for 𝔖 (62).

For M there is no discrete model, so the factorisation M → M^Δ(Ẑ) must be imposed as an axiom of the Lie tower. Using that M_Q/M_Q° is constant, he defines the adelic analogue M_Q^Δ(A_Q) and requires that M → M_Q(A_Q) factor through it (eq. (63), next page).

Next page: he then adds two requirements:
- the images of (62) are open, an analogue of open-image and congruence-subgroup properties;
- the composites to the γ's are surjective.
With all conditions satisfied he speaks of a 'non-degenerate integral Lie situation'.

Purpose: an arithmetic, adelic 'Lie' (algebraic-group) hull of the Teichmüller-Galois tower. It is analogous to the Zariski closure or Mumford-Tate group of the image of Galois, with an integral structure over Z.
errors: No mathematical error. (62) silently needs two facts: Π (resp. 𝔖) is the profinite completion of Π_0 (or Π_0 has dense image), and Π^Δ(Ẑ) is closed in Π(Ẑ). Both hold in the intended setting.
Exactness of (61) is plausible only on the right (quotients of finite groups), as written. It is not exactness on the left; the original wording of (60) as 'exacte' was correctly struck out.

ideas.what: Constancy of the component group schemes Π/Π° over Spec Z, and the 'diagonal' subgroup of adelic points G^Δ(Ẑ) = preimage of diagonal γ ⊂ ∏_p γ.
ideas.modern_name: Adelic points with ℓ-independent component; independence of ℓ of the component group of ℓ-adic monodromy groups; the field K^conn
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (letter to Ribet, 1981; Résumé des cours 1984-85); Larsen-Pink (1990s) for ℓ-independence results
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Requirement that the arithmetic group M (Galois-Teichmüller) map into M_Q^Δ(A_Q), i.e. Galois acts compatibly on component groups at all places at once.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility condition for adelic Galois images, a Mumford-Tate-type framework for the Galois action on the profinite Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (open image, adelic Galois images); Hain-Matsumoto (weighted completions of arithmetic mapping class groups, 2003)

ideas.what: Third-isomorphism-theorem diagram of component groups (61) for the tower Π ⊂ 𝔖 ⊂ M with quotients Σ, N, T.
ideas.modern_name: Exact sequences of π_0 of algebraic group hulls

ideas.what: Automatic factorisation of the profinite completion through G^Δ(Ẑ) because the discrete group lands in G(Z).

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, as an axiom on a 'Lie tower' of the Galois-Teichmüller group, the diagonal-component condition. This is the requirement that the map to π_0 of the adelic hull is independent of the place. It is essentially the condition Serre isolated (independence of ℓ of the component group and of K^conn) for ℓ-adic Galois images, here transplanted to the anabelian/Teichmüller setting over Spec Z.
missed.quote: Cette hypothèse sur Π, 𝔖, M permet de définir des groupes Π^Δ(Ẑ), 𝔖^Δ(Ẑ), M^Δ(Ẑ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and adelic algebraic hulls of Galois actions on mapping class groups (Hain-Matsumoto weighted completions) are usually treated one prime at a time. An integral, all-places 'Lie situation' with diagonal component condition and open image is a cleaner global formulation that seems not to have been developed.

missed.claim: Definition of a 'non-degenerate integral Lie situation' for a Teichmüller-Galois structure: group schemes over Z, constant π_0, diagonal factorisation, open images, surjectivity onto components. Grothendieck lists the axioms but does not construct examples or prove existence here.
missed.quote: Quant à la troisième factorisation, elle devrait être incluse dans les conditions de définition d'une tour de Lie d'une structure de Teichmüller-Galois
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Constructing such integral Lie towers (e.g. from symplectic or motivic representations of arithmetic mapping class groups) remains open in this generality.

deep.surprise_reason: The diagonal-component adelic subgroup and the global integral 'Lie tower' axioms for the Galois-Teichmüller tower are a neat, unpublished formalisation. They parallel Serre's roughly contemporaneous ℓ-independence ideas, but are formal axioms rather than results.
transcription_corrections: Throughout (59)-(61) the handwriting has lowercase γ (γ_Π, γ_𝔖, γ_M, γ_Σ, γ_N, γ_T), matching the underlined γ of eq. (58), not uppercase Γ.
In (62) and the following text the superscript is a small triangle Δ (diagonal); stray extra superscripts after Π^Δ(Ẑ) and 𝔖^Δ(Ẑ) in the image are corrections, not separate symbols.
Last line: 'M_Q / M_Q°' with underlined M, consistent with (58).
